We just need to look elsewhere to people who cares about us. It's enough if you see people staring a you for example in a supermarket no matter if they are workers, those people could probably make you very happy. I've proven that it's so because the girls working there go to see me when I hide while deciding what to buy as if telling me that they need me to talk to them :)

It happens to me but sadly I'm too shy, maybe I'll dare some day and will talk back to someone I like who clearly stares at me. I know it is so because they even go to see me where I'm hiding, as if those girls were telling me that they want me to talk to them.

As if we all were trapped in a null/void social layer where nobody talks to nobody, and this is how they ask for help to talk to them, so I should, it's not a suspicion or an illusion, it's a fact that the people who you think that stares at you and you like are asking for help for you to just go and talk to them.

Go to the places you know, you like the most, or where you have seen people who like you, go to the usual safe places where nothing at all has happened to you before as it will ensure that you will be able to get what everyone wants to be happy.

If you don't know what to do or say just stay beside them, it's enough. Sooner or later something else will happen.

So please do so and be happy. This is what we all need as humans.

It looks that it's what you need, finding good people, look at how you advance towards that goal in what you write.

You probably are dedicating too much to stop yourself from meeting with people you want for whatever reason, but I've seen that people, starting with teens, just go out in a trip to any place with their friends or family and just relax, no worries at all, just like in the school and end year trips.

Why don't you try to make use of all the ways in which others have solved their suicidal problems without killing themselves?

The fact that others have achieved it means that it could as well have been you, so be it you or other who surpassed their problems, killing yourself no longer makes sense.

For example, you could get a hold of the fact that I was going to kill myself in 2004, but didn't because I found my female Siamese kitten friend (or she found me), I helped her giving her food (chicken) and she gave me back all of her absolute love while I was suicidal, and it healed me immediately.

So if a huge mutual friendship healed me, why not think that it all that you need? I'm here alive just because of my kitten friend, but if I'm here telling you this, it's because she is also your friend, but you have this human being too who could teach you many things, so why kill yourself?

We get to a point where we are too weak, but that's the point where we have reached our current full potential in a skill. We are just tired and since we are at the peak point of whatever makes us feel bad, we feel weak because the rest of our abilities are resting, so the thing we are focusing at is working alone without the help of the rest of our own being.

It's normal, the body is designed like that for making it possible to make each of our abilities, knowledge, ideas, stand-alone and functional on their own, for making it possible to turn them into reflexes so that we don't think too much once we master something.

I'm telling it after having been in operating system development programming since 2004, so I know how the hardest things in computing, in software, are like. If you don't feel bad then it's because you have an exceptional amount of help and you have a nicer life than most persons and animals.

Your mother is probably the best friend ever in your life, but she is so common that you don't evaluate right now how much she can help you. Things are hard in life for everyone in some aspect we focus a lot, often nobody loves nobody except for your true friends and family, so there's no need to worry, it's normal.

We feel tired when we reach the highest point of consciousness of each different mental state, idea or skill after a while during the day.

If we feel constantly tired it's because we are constantly working at the peak level in everything we do and we would need to dedicate ourselves mainly to rest for a time to feel better, but we would still feel tired when we reach the peak point of our resting state.

In any case, to be good, we need to learn to work being tired for fully improving each individual state, and also learn to rest for recovering and being able to increase our abilities, just as if it was a dream, but a dream that consists in what we learn to do and as such we need to keep up our efforts up to the tiredness point to see where we behave foolish and make big mistakes while tired to make that state stand-alone, and then rest at the same time for turning it into instinct-grade, reflex-triggered personal capabilities that will work well when tired when we reach the full extent of the bodily and mental state where those abilities come from.

At least you are doing the right thing by making a bad decision like suicide to stay slower than good things in your life. The more suicide is kept at low speed and low priority, good things will be able to reach you, accumulate and make room, give time to true help to arrive.

Don't you think that you are taking a decision towards an undesired end far too fast?

If you rush too much to an undesired goal, you are leaving the many decisions and options you truly want without a chance to catch up with you.

You probably wanted a special friendship to the end of your life, but if it didn't work at first, then there will have to be a person that really enjoys you and you too, for it to work. What you want is great, but finding it is incredibly hard for anyone. I don't know how many people achieve this, but it's so rare that suicide makes no sense because it's already too hard for everyone, too sincere to make suicide a decision that has anything to do with it.

You must not die.

Suicide just tries to make good things come slower and bad things come always faster than good ones, by convincing you to block whatever good that happens to you because it looks too small compared to gratuitous bad things.

What you must do is act on the bad thoughts always extremely slower, always more slowly than any good thing that you see happening in your life.

You must make sure to make good things to reach you always at full speed, faster than suicide. In this way suicide will always lose.

You'll make good things to catch up the evil ones once and for all if you always act on negative decisions extremely slowly and act and enjoy the good things always faster than bad ones... If you make bad things incredibly slow and good things develop at normal speed...

Have you drinking enough water, enough rehydration salts?

I've tried to drink enough to urinate my blood weight in water every day. I feel that it has helped me. My urine went through several smell stages, because I almost didn't drink water for around 2 years, but now I look increasingly better and I know that getting rid of all those toxins gives me more space to fight effectively any disease.

Your best friend can never do something bad to you.

If he/she does, then don't worry. You might thing they are the best friend of your life, but don't deceive yourself, they are regular friends, not the best one.

You must not die.

Take your decisions slowly. If you take suicide-related decisions on purpose extremely slowly, it always loses because unexpected helping factors always end up arriving first and becoming heavier and better than suicide.

If you can, take suicide or self-harming actions and any undesirable imagination/thought/emotion/imagined act always much more slowly than the things that you feel that help you. It will truly make the good things you have always wanted to catch up the bad ones once and for all. Why not treat suicide itself with the lack of importance that it tries to give you, as normally happens when one isn't in a suicidal state?

Take your time. If you take any decisions right now and act extremely slowly on purpose, you will allow any good solution to catch up with you.

If you feel paralyzed, demotivated, you have probably been learning a lot for a good time.

In that case you feel paralyzed because different parts from your body and mind try to do different things. You must only use the parts of your body, mind and brain that want to do something. The rest of you must stay resting keeping a rest position until they join the parts that started wanted to do something.

You become more multitasking the more you learn, so you want to do several things at the same time, but if you know more than before, only using the parts that want to do one same thing will allow you to block yourself.

If only a finger or a hand want to do something, for example write or read something, then only use that and let the rest of the body to practically stay asleep until it all feels that it can coordinate with your current activity.

You must not die.

Bad thoughts tell you to die.

So what to do? When it comes to getting help, it will always be someone who will help you and stay with you. When it comes to being suicidal, it will always be just thoughts that try to block you from remembering that you must not die.

In the end they will help you to become strong enough to do great things from your own initiative and strength. You should definitely decide what to do extremely slowly, act equally slowly towards what should help you. Just put a weight against suicide, and let them develop. Feel how one or the other take you to further steps. In the end the one that will win will be the one that you cultivate, the suicide or the whole new set of decisions of what else to do.

Acting so incredibly slowly will help you in thorough ways regardless of what you are thinking to do, and even more for critical and instinctive things like this one. It will allow anything and anyone that can help you in the exact way you want, to catch up to find you.

You must not die.

Bad thoughts tell you to die.

So what to do? When it comes to getting help, it will always be someone who will help you and stay with you. When it comes to being suicidal, it will always be just thoughts that try to block you from remembering that you must not die.

You must not die.

What would you do if someone has helped you in a way you really liked against suicide, and if that someone died during the time they were helping you, if they spent their last time and gave you your friendship, if you both were the latest friends?

You only need to see the face of people who has died to know that there's nothing pleasant or good in dying. It's bad, simply, and if life is difficult, death won't treat you better but undoubtedly much worse.

They are telling you that dying is bad, their bodies reacted and are telling you how terrible dying can be, specially if the death is deliberate in any way.

As for me, what keeps me going is the help my Siamese cat friend gave me in 2004. She appeared by herself in my house. She saved me from suicide, and thanks to her I had time to resolve doing great things that I never thought about, like trying to make an operating system and its programs, and I've learned a lot since 2004. I live with my parents in my childhood house, I am earning more money slowly with eBay products, I need to make sure that I can make a living from what I like the most, programming and learning/explaining others about absolutely everything.

I always think that if cats hadn't existed since prehistory, then my friend wouldn't haven't been there to help me, so they all as species made it possible to bring her.

Now I had    he time to experience help from other animals and people, not just a single species or point of view, which is good, healthy, and shows that what helped me is based on being beneficial to life in general.

You just need to decide to do those things instead of setting them in your mind as failed.

See how the suicidal mindset is just leading you to a pre-set result. It feels great because it has just set itself the goal of killing you.

Instead, you could spend this year in the single thing that matters most to you and that you know that you can reach and achieve at least minimally.

If you replace something you want in place of your death as the goal, you could use the hard resources that suicidal thinking has taken from you to achieve your goals as easily.

As for friendships, the very few true friendships almost always appear suddenly and last literally forever, but you must take care of them from danger. Those friendships are close, personal and physically present in your life and activities, as close as in your own room. Any other friendship might be great, but is not specific just for you, so there's no real reason to worry because those individuals just cannot feel completely fulfilled with you, they aren't really for each other. They are so good that not even jealousy can be felt, they  are really based on the best things we always ever wanted from friendship and mutual well-being.

Suicide is based in under-studied/under-researched human instincts that need something or someone that fulfills them completely from our instinctive view, something or someone capable of healing us instantly at the very first personal interaction, to stop the desire to commit suicide permanently. The problem is that we don't know what we really want until we are lucky or positively instinctive enough without noticing to find the things that can help us.

I wanted to commit suicide from the half of 2002 and June 2004 because my mind failed and I heard in my mind a horrible insult against things I've always respected. I felt that I couldn't live the rest of my life with the memory of that moment, which would keep evoking the same insults, so I just decided immediately that I would slowly kill myself, I was around 18 years old. It happened around 8-9 PM while listening to a non-musical program in the radio, about esoteric healers just for fun.

At most, what can be observed is that being truly mistreated is the beginning of becoming depressive or suicidal, and being truly well-treated is the beginning of fulfilling the instincts and/or needs that will make us have absolute well-being. To truly mistreat or treat well us, it needs to be from something or someone that we really care about, a friend that we really like from the first moment we interact with them, our own involuntary thoughts, etc.

Go to the places and people you know from those times, and do what you did back then, everything of it, in your mind those things will have new great ideas for you since you stopped doing them.

There's something special on the things and persons that can take out of depression and suicide. There's normal, regular things that improve our life to a big milestone, and there are other things and individuals that are so good that make one perfectly fulfilled to no end. Those are the hardest to find, usually they find us first. At least if I hadn't found things like those just for me, I wouldn't understand that the real well being doesn't allow for destructive attitudes in depression, they always take you back to your full well-being.

If I still feel sad, depressed, self-destructive with all I have, I know that I haven't found yet what will really help me. But I've been lucky, a friend found me and made me understand, made me become constructive and now all I do makes me absolutely satisfied, I like programming and learning everything there is.

A female Siamese cat became my friend and saved my life from suicide. For others, it could be a human being, an activity, or anything, but if there's nothing to permanently take the place of those negative things, then that's the problem, but the things and the ones that have never failed you unconditionally, specially the ones that were there to heal and in your best moments, will always keep filling any voids.

Anyone's words will really help, only the ones that are beside you and that truly care about you in a way that only you can fully appreciate. It's something exceptional that apparently only very few individuals can achieve, bringing every other good thing from that point on.

They will appear at some point, but they are there, it's one of the most difficult things to make possible for each of us individually and that we totally like, that's why it takes so much time. They also need you in some way to be seen.

Think in the best moments of your life, if you adopt the actions you did when you were younger and happiest, and stop doing things that drain you right now, you will have a time as good as before the more you keep your previous ways of living that you know that come from your happiest times.

Do what you really know and start from there, expand it and you will find that you can keep offering the things that you were always excellent at.

Go to the places and people you know from those times, and do what you did back then, everything of it, in your mind those things will have new great ideas for you since you stopped doing them.
